{
"Reactive Programming": "A declarative programming paradigm centered on data streams and the automatic propagation of changes, enabling systems to react to events, inputs, or state changes over time.",
"Data Stream": "A continuous, time-ordered sequence of data elements that can be processed incrementally as values become available.",
"Propagation of Changes": "The mechanism by which modifications to a data source are automatically forwarded through dependent computations and subscribers in a reactive system.",
"Observable": "A reactive abstraction representing a data source that emits a sequence of values, errors, or completion signals to which observers can subscribe.",
"Data Source": "An entity, system, or component that produces data values which can be exposed as a stream or observable for downstream consumption.",
"Stream": "An abstract sequence of asynchronous events or values that flows from a producer to one or more consumers over time.",
"Asynchronous Event": "A discrete occurrence or value emitted independently of the caller's execution flow, delivered at a non-deterministic point in time.",
"Operator": "A function that transforms, combines, or filters observables and streams, producing a new stream as output while preserving reactive semantics.",
"Map Operator": "An operator that applies a transformation function to each emitted value, producing a new stream of transformed values.",
"Filter Operator": "An operator that selectively forwards only those emitted values that satisfy a given predicate, discarding the rest.",
"FlatMap Operator": "An operator that maps each emitted value to an inner observable and flattens the resulting streams into a single output stream.",
"Subscription": "A connection established between an observer and an observable that enables the flow of emissions and can be used to cancel or dispose of the stream.",
"Observer": "A consumer that subscribes to an observable to receive its emitted values, error notifications, and completion signals.",
"Backpressure": "A flow-control mechanism that allows consumers to signal and regulate the rate at which producers emit data to prevent overload.",
"Consumer": "A component that subscribes to and processes values emitted by a stream or observable, acting as the endpoint of the reactive pipeline.",
"Emission Rate": "The frequency or speed at which an observable or stream produces values for its subscribers over time."
}
